correctness.rationale: Character degree j has Laplacian eigenvalue 2j; summing the character signs at each distance gives the four exact rows. Diagonal and distance-one entries are positive, and ordinary product heat plus positive subordination yields strict positivity for 0<alpha<=1. Set a=2^alpha, b=4^alpha, c=6^alpha. The derivative of the distance-two numerator, multiplied by exp(ct), is a exp((c−a)t)+b exp((c−b)t)−c, strictly increasing and negative initially for alpha>1. This gives one positive crossing. For distance three an exponential sum with four distinct exponents has at most three real zeros with multiplicity (divide out one term and induct by Rolle). Its initial slope divided by a is 3−3*2^alpha+3^alpha; this three-term sum has its two roots at alpha=1 and 2 and is negative between, positive above. At alpha=2 the time-zero root is double with second derivative −576. For 1<alpha<=2, the negative initial sign and positive limit force one simple positive zero by the count and sign parity. For alpha>2 the initial sign is positive, but the entry is negative at (log 2)/b and tends to a positive limit, giving exactly two simple positive zeros. At (log 2)/b the distance-two numerator is also negative, using b/a>=4 and c/b>=9/4; at (log 2)/a it is positive while the distance-three numerator is negative. Thus the negative intervals overlap and entrywise nonnegativity returns exactly at the later distance-three zero, with the isolated t=0 case. At t=u/b and t=v/a the antipodal numerators tend to −2+3 exp(−u) and 1−3 exp(−v), yielding the two constants by brackets. For the middle zero u=bt_2 and p=b/a, evaluating between (1±epsilon)log p gives u~log p, then (1−exp(−u/p))exp(u)=1−exp(−(c/b−1)u) gives u exp(u)/p→1. The slope of u+log u is >=1, giving the stronger additive o(1) Lambert remainder.
residual_risks: All root counts are analytic; the recorded floating-point comparisons are not a root-count certificate. The result is specific to the unweighted combinatorial Q3 Laplacian and does not classify higher cubes.

value.rationale: The three-cube is the first cube with the distance-three entry needed for this question. Its antipodal positive–negative–positive pattern disappears when testing positivity of the full matrix because the distance-two obstruction overlaps the antipodal interval. Separating the three characteristic times, including a logarithmically enhanced middle scale, quantifies what an eventual-positivity criterion or a single antipodal test misses on this natural graph.
residual_risks: The mechanism has an analogous manifestation on P4; value here rests on the exact quantitative Q3 distinction, not on claiming unique or graph-universal reentrance.
